cSkillsWhat: Ways of working Claude reads when needed (instructions plus helper files). Each is downloaded at a pinned version into this folder.
cManualWhat: License unclear, so not copied automatically. After setup Claude walks you through installing them in the terminal.
cHooksWhatNoPlugin: This file only lists which hooks are on. Hooks run only in Claude Code with the harness-fit plugin installed — it is not installed yet, so nothing is blocked for now.
cHooksWhat: The hooks are run by the harness-fit plugin you already installed. This file only lists which hooks are on. Right before Claude runs a command or writes a file, it checks and blocks violations.
cRulesWhat: Project instructions Claude reads at the start of every conversation. Existing text stays; only a marked block is added.
cShareWhat: When teammates open this repo in Claude Code they are prompted to install harness-fit ({repo} {ref}). Existing settings stay.
cNoteWhat: Saves your requests. After setup Claude reads and applies them, then tells you what changed.
cExploreWhat: After setup Claude reads them and tells you whether they're worth using.
cGitHookWhat: Right before git commits, it re-runs the harness-fit write hooks (secrets, .env, unsafe HTML, version ranges, workflows, large new files) on what is actually being committed, including files written from the shell or other tools. It lives inside .git, so it is not committed; on teammates' machines the hooks inside Claude Code cover commits instead.
cBackupWhat: Saves the original of every file that changes (one .gitignore line keeps it out of commits). Used for undo.
stepsTitle: After you press Apply, this happens in order
step1: Back up the files that will change
step2: Write the settings files and CLAUDE.md
step4: Go back to the terminal. Claude summarizes the result and continues with what's left (manual installs, your requests)

ghTitle: Also turn on GitHub repository settings
ghD: Enforces the branch strategy on GitHub's servers too, so merging from the web UI or with gh api is blocked as well. Leave it off and GitHub stays as it is.
ghShared: {repo} · applies to everyone who uses this repository
ghPickHint: Turn on to choose {n} {n|setting|settings} one by one. The recommended ones are preselected.
ghNoneSelected: Nothing selected, so GitHub stays as it is
ghNeedsPr: Turn on "require a pull request" to choose this
ghh_squash: Each PR becomes one commit, so history stays tidy. The merge-commit and rebase buttons go away.
ghh_autodelete: GitHub deletes the branch once its PR is merged. Turn off if your team keeps using branches after merging.
ghh_pullRequest: No direct pushes to that branch; changes go through PRs. If you used to push directly, you will open a PR every time.
ghh_approvals: With 0 you can merge your own PR alone. With 1 or more someone else must approve, so a solo repository can no longer merge.
ghh_noForcePush: Stops overwriting pushed history. A bad commit has to be fixed with a revert commit.
ghh_noDelete: Stops the remote branch from being deleted by accident.
ghh_enforceAdmins: Even you, as an admin, cannot push straight to that branch. Off lets admins bypass the protection rules above.
ghLoading: Checking whether GitHub repository settings can be turned on…
ghNotOffered: GitHub repository settings are not available: {reason}
ghAlready: The GitHub repository settings ({repo}) already match this branch strategy.
ghReason_not-github: this is not a GitHub repository (origin is not on github.com)
ghReason_not-logged-in: gh is not logged in (gh auth login)
ghReason_offline: cannot reach GitHub (check your internet connection)
ghReason_not-found: GitHub could not find this repository
ghReason_no-admin: you do not have admin permission on this repository
ghReason_no-settings: this branch strategy has no GitHub settings to change
ghReason_error: could not read the GitHub settings

cGithubWhat: These change on GitHub's servers, not on your computer, for everyone who uses this repository. They are changed after the files are written.

ghResultNone: GitHub repository settings were not changed: {reason}

applyPreviewFailed: Can't apply: the changes could not be worked out
applyNeedShare: Answer the teammate question to apply
teamQ: Should teammates get the same hooks?
teamQD: “Yes” adds a harness-fit install prompt to .claude/settings.json. When a teammate opens this repo in Claude Code, they are asked to install it. “No” keeps it on this PC only.
teamStep1: After applying, commit and push these files.
teamStep2: When a teammate pulls the repo, opens it in Claude Code and trusts the folder, they are asked to install harness-fit ({repo} {ref}).
teamStep3: Once they install it, the same hooks run for their Claude too. Nothing runs before that.
teamStep4: The git pre-commit hook (.git/hooks/pre-commit) is not part of the repo.
teamStep4D: So commits a teammate makes by hand, without Claude, are not checked as is. If they open /harness-fit:setup on their own PC and apply as is (it starts from the last selection), the same hook goes into their .git/hooks. Until then, hooks only see commits made inside Claude Code.
budgetNearT: The skill list is close to its budget
budgetOverT: The skill list may go over its budget
budgetWhy: Claude always sees a list of skill names and descriptions and picks skills from it. Over budget, new skills lose their descriptions first, so Claude may not pick them on its own. You can still call them with `/name`.
budgetHeavy: Even without the new skills, the skills you already have use {pct}% of the budget. Turning off plugins you do not use helps.
budgetRaise: To raise the budget, add `"skillListingBudgetFraction": 0.02` (2% of the context window) to settings.json. It costs that many more tokens in every conversation. harness-fit does not change your settings.
doneCmdsD: Claude picks them up on its own, or call one by name. The Skills line in `/context` shows the real size.
doneCmdsBudget: The skill list is close to its budget, so Claude may not pick these up on its own once descriptions are dropped. Call them by name. The Skills line in `/context` shows the real size.
budgetPastT: The skill list is over its budget
applyFailNone: No files were changed (anything written was put back right away). Fix the cause and apply again. Your previous setup is untouched.

applyFsBusy: Another program is using the file. Close it and apply again.
